record.paper_title: Graph Partitions: Recent Progresses and Some Open Problems
record.original_question: Let s be a positive integer. Does every graph with minimum degree at least 2s + 1 admit a bisection (S, T) such that both induced subgraphs G[S] and G[T] have minimum degree at least s?

evidence.quote: In the light of the connection to Conjecture 3.3, we propose the following, perhaps easier, question on gb(s, s).
Problem 4.1[45] Let s be a positive integer. Is it true that every graph with minimum degree at least 2s + 1 admits a bisection (S, T ) such that min{δ(G[S]), δ(G[T ])} ≥ s?
If the answer is YES, then the bound is best possible as evidenced by the complete graph K2s+1.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $s$ be a positive integer. A bisection of a graph $G=(V,E)$ on $n$ vertices is an ordered partition $(S,T)$ of $V$ with $\lvert\,|S|-|T|\,\rvert\le 1$. For a subset $U\subseteq V$, let $G[U]$ denote the subgraph of $G$ induced by $U$, and let $\delta(H)$ denote the minimum degree of a graph $H$. 

Determine whether the following statement is true: every finite simple graph $G$ with minimum degree $\delta(G)\ge 2s+1$ admits a bisection $(S,T)$ such that 
$$\min\{\delta(G[S]),\ \delta(G[T])\}\ \ge\ s.$$
(If true, the bound $2s+1$ on the minimum degree is best possible, as shown by the complete graph $K_{2s+1}$.)
artifact.status_search_result: Recent works on bisections of graphs under degree constraints (including arXiv:2504.15096, 2025) address related but distinct problems—achieving constant-fraction internal-degree conditions rather than the absolute threshold δ(G[S]),δ(G[T])≥s under δ(G)≥2s+1. No source found resolves this specific question, which continues to be cited as an open problem in the area of judicious bipartitions.

status_evidence.title: Bisections of graphs under degree constraints
status_evidence.snippet: Establishes bisections where each vertex has ≥(1/4−o(1))d_G(v) neighbors in its own part; does not give absolute minimum-degree guarantees in the induced parts.
status_evidence.claim: The 2s+1 → δ(G[S]),δ(G[T])≥s bisection question is not settled by this recent work.

status_evidence.title: On problems about judicious bipartitions of graphs
status_evidence.snippet: Studies judicious bipartition problems related to minimum-degree bisection thresholds.
status_evidence.claim: The general s-good bisection question with δ(G)≥2s+1 remains a problem of interest.
